name: Will a pool renovation help with algae and maintenance problems?

mainEntity.name: Can renovating an old pool reduce algae buildup and constant maintenance?
mainEntity.text: Can renovating an old pool reduce algae buildup and constant maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: A renovation can absolutely improve recurring maintenance issues, but only if the underlying cause is addressed. Rough or aging surfaces can hold algae more easily, while poor circulation, weak filtration, failing pumps, or hidden leaks can make maintenance a constant struggle. New plaster or pebble finish, updated tile and coping, and more efficient equipment can create a pool that is easier to keep clean and chemically balanced. If the pool has dead spots, poor return placement, or outdated hydraulics, those issues should be corrected during the renovation rather than ignored. Homeowners who are tired of constant brushing and chemical adjustments should ask for an evaluation of both surface condition and system performance. Renovation works best when it improves the pool as a system, not just its appearance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, renovation can help if algae and maintenance problems are caused by rough surfaces, poor circulation, failing equipment, or leaks. Fresh finishes, updated plumbing, and better filtration can make the pool easier to clean and keep balanced.
